text.p: Turkish lira firmed to 114,825 against the dollar on Friday after steadying at 115,000 levels on Thursday, in line with the the dollar's drop in world markets, bankers said.
They said the dollar traded in a limited range as banks kept to the sidelines due to a volatile dollar/mark parity.
The lira has lost 1.7 percent of its value against the dollar this week.

The central bank drained 2.6 trillion lira of idle cash from banks at 54 percent overnight towards the close, but also lent banks 1.6 trillion lira overnight at 74 percent due to cash demand which remained strong earlier in the day.

Bankers said banks' liquidity needs for the weekend buoyed lira demand earlier in the day after the market opened 12.3 trillion lira short. But idle cash, left after banks' demands were met, was withdrawn by the central bank.
The bank also lent 600 billion lira at 69 percent via tomorrow/next deals.
The average overnight money rose to 71.2 percent from 65.02 percent on Thursday when the central bank lent a total of five trillion lira via overnight and t/n deals.
Yields on the most heavily traded bonds dropped by one and two points after Thursday's rise while yields on some other papers edged higher.

The average yield on the most active October 30 paper was 88.45 percent, down 1.1 points from 89.55 percent on Thursday. The second most active February 11, 1998 paper yielded 86.54 percent, down from 88.62 percent Thursday average.
The average overnight repo rate firmed to 75.59 percent from Thursday's 71.53 amid cash squeeze in the day.
